title: Show session directory
description:
Add `session.directory` (fall back to `session.path`) to results.

- Human view: show the directory line (e.g. alongside slug).
- `--json`: expose a `directory` field.
- Implement now against the existing TS prototype.

Note: filtering/scoping by directory belongs to the search & scoping epic; this ticket is display-only.

Acceptance: directory shown in human + json for `cotails <term>` and `--title-only`.
notes:
Implemented in opencotails.ts:
- Added `directory` to both SELECTs (buildTitleQuery: `directory`; buildPartQuery: `s.directory AS directory`).
- renderHuman now shows `slug · directory` on the meta line (grey).
- `--json` exposes `directory` automatically (whole row is serialized).

Verified: human + --title-only + --json all surface the session directory (e.g. `/home/rektide/src/opencotails`).

title: Information gathering & display
description:
Surface the metadata, timeline, and lineage around opencode sessions so a user can orient on *what a session is and how it came to be* — not just whether it matches a search term.

Today `cotails` reports only `id`, `slug`, `title`, `updated`, and a text `snippet`. The opencode schema carries far richer signal that is currently invisible (all on the `session` table unless noted):

- **Provenance:** `time_created` (when it began), `directory` / `path` (where), `project_id` -> `project.name`.
- **Fork lineage:** `fork_session_id` + `fork_message_id` — the parent session and the exact message at which this session diverged.
- **Lifecycle:** `time_compacting`, `time_suspended`, `time_archived`.
- **Cost/usage:** `cost`, `tokens_input`, `tokens_output`, `tokens_reasoning`, `tokens_cache_read`/`write`.

This epic owns **reporting** — reading these fields and rendering them in both human and `--json` output. It does NOT own the matching/query side (search & scoping epic) or the FTS index (index epic).

## Scope (children)
- `cotail-created-at` — first `time_created`.
- `cotail-fork-time` — last fork time.
- `cotail-fork-point` — the previous prompt+reply and fork prompt+reply around the fork boundary, with timestamps.
- `cotail-directory` — the session directory (implement first).

## Out of scope
- Search semantics, scoping filters, FTS index, Rust port (separate epics).

title: Live session discovery via opencode HTTP server + mDNS
description:
# Discover the active opencode session over HTTP (with mDNS), not /proc heuristics

## Why

`cotail-get-session` (shipped) resolves an opencode PID → active session by
reading `/proc/<pid>/cwd` and matching the **most recently updated** session
in that directory. That works, but it is a heuristic: it can mis-pick when
several opencode instances share a directory, it cannot distinguish a busy
session from a merely-recent one, and it is Linux-only. opencode **already**
exposes precise live state over an HTTP server — we just have to turn it on
and point cotails at it.

## What opencode already supports (researched against `~/a/a/v2`, v1 secondary)

**The TUI starts a real HTTP server when asked to.** In v2
(`packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:233-249`):

```
const external = hasArg("--port") || hasArg("--hostname") || network.mdns === true
const transport = external
  ? { url: (await client.call("server", network)).url, ... }   // real HTTP listener
  : { url: "http://opencode.internal", fetch: createWorkerFetch(client), ... }  // in-process RPC only
```

So `opencode --mdns` (or `--port N` / `--hostname 0.0.0.0`) launches the TUI
**with a live HTTP API**. v1 has the identical mechanism
(`cli/tui/worker.ts` `server` RPC). `opencode serve` / `opencode web` start a
headless server the same way.

**mDNS** (`server/mdns.ts`): when enabled, publishes a service
`opencode-<port>`, type `http`, host `opencode.local` (override with
`--mdns-domain`), txt `{path:"/"}` via `bonjour-service`. Enabling `--mdns`
defaults the hostname to `0.0.0.0`.

**Flags + config** (`cli/network.ts`): `--port` (default 0 = prefer 4096 then
free), `--hostname`, `--mdns`, `--mdns-domain`, `--cors`. `serve`/`web` also
read `config.server.{port,hostname,mdns,mdnsDomain,cors}` from opencode.json.
(Note: the **TUI** path calls `resolveNetworkOptionsNoConfig` with no config,
so for the TUI these are **flag-only** today — a gotcha to document.)

**Endpoints that pin down the *active* session** (the whole point):
- `GET /session/status` → `{sessionID → {type: idle|busy|…}}`. Non-idle entries
  are the sessions actively running right now — a direct "active" signal the
  /proc heuristic cannot see. (`session/status.ts`: idle entries are dropped,
  so the map holds only busy sessions.)
- `GET /project/current` → the currently active project.
- `GET /session/{id}` and `/session/{id}/message` → full `SessionInfo` + message
  counts (feeds layer 8 of `cotail-session-report`).

## Deliverables

1. **Launch wrapper / docs** — a small script (e.g. an `oc-serve` shim or a
   documented alias) that starts `opencode --mdns` (v2; v1 fallback documented)
   so a server is always present. Record the gotchas (TUI = flag-only; set
   `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`; mDNS host `opencode.local`).
2. **mDNS discovery in cotails** — browse for `opencode-<port>`/`http` services
   to find running instances without a hardcoded port (a `bonjour-service`/mdns
   lookup, or scan the known 4096+ range as a fallback).
3. **HTTP resolver in `get-session`** — add an `--http <url>` / `--mdns` mode to
   `cotails get-session` that queries `/session/status` (+`/project/current`)
   for the active session, falling back to the existing `/proc` resolver when no
   server is found. This makes the resolver cross-platform and exact.
4. **Live fields** — pipe `/session/status` + message counts into the
   `SessionInfo` "live" layer (layer 8 of `cotail-session-report`).

## Direction across existing work

- **`cotail-get-session` (done)**: current `/proc` resolver becomes the offline
  fallback; HTTP becomes primary when a server is reachable.
- **`cotail-session-report`**: this ticket is the source of its layer-8 (live)
  fields — status, message count, last activity.
- **`cotail-history`**: could later annotate which sessions are live/busy.

## Acceptance

- A documented, scripted way to run opencode with HTTP+mDNS on (v2; v1 noted).
- `cotails get-session --mdns` (or `--http`) returns the *busy* session from a
  running instance, cross-platform.
- Falls back to `/proc` when no server/mDNS answer.
- Security note documented (auth/password, binding to localhost vs 0.0.0.0).

## Open questions

- Does opencode expose the TUI's *currently-selected* (viewed) session, or only
  *busy* ones, over HTTP? `TuiEvent.SessionSelect` is published on switch
  (`handlers/tui.ts`) — an event stream may be needed to track "viewed" vs
  "running". Confirm during implementation.
notes: Upstream intent: the TUI network-config gap is an opencode oversight worth fixing upstream, not papering over in cotails. tui.ts:233 calls resolveNetworkOptionsNoConfig(args) (no config); switching to the config-aware resolveNetworkOptions(args) (as serve/web already do) would make server.{mdns,port,hostname,mdnsDomain,cors} in opencode.json apply to the TUI — giving env/config-based mDNS with no wrapper or alias. This is the preferred path; the shell alias (alias opencode='opencode --mdns') is only an interim workaround until that one-line upstream lands. Track in ~/src/doc/opencode-patches.md.

title: Define a consolidated core session report format (SessionInfo)
description:
# Consolidate a canonical "session report" shape

`cotails` is growing several read-side tickets that each surface slices of
session data (`cotail-basic-fields`, `cotail-fork-point`, `cotail-fork-time`,
the just-shipped `cotail-get-session`). They all need the **same** object to
hang fields off. This epic owns the **one** definition of that object so the
slices compose instead of diverging.

## Current state (already landed)

`cotail-get-session` introduced `src/opencode/session-info.ts` with a minimal
`SessionInfo`:

```
id, title, directory, slug, projectId, parentId, version, timeCreated, timeUpdated
```

That is **layer 1 (core)** below. This epic promotes it to the full report.

## Proposed layered schema

All fields camelCase in the public `--json` shape; mapped from snake_case DB
columns in the query layer (see `mapRow` in `session-info.ts`). Optional
layers load lazily — core is always present, the rest behind flags or
populated by the ticket that owns them.

| layer | fields | source | owning ticket |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 core** (done) | id, title, directory, slug, projectId, parentId, version, timeCreated, timeUpdated | `session` table | cotail-get-session ✓ |
| **2 run** | model, agent | `session.model`, `session.agent` | cotail-basic-fields |
| **3 cost** | cost, tokens{input,output,reasoning,cacheRead,cacheWrite} | `session.cost`, `session.tokens_*` | cotail-basic-fields |
| **4 vcs** | summary{additions,deletions,files,diffs} | `session.summary_*` | cotail-basic-fields |
| **5 fork** | forkSessionId, forkMessageId, forkPoint{messageId,time}, forkTime | `session.fork_*` + message joins | cotail-fork-point, cotail-fork-time |
| **6 share** | shareUrl | `session.share_url` | cotail-basic-fields |
| **7 lifecycle** | timeCompacting, timeArchived, timeSuspended | `session.time_*` | (this epic / later) |
| **8 live** (HTTP only) | status{idle/busy/…}, messageCount, lastMessage | opencode HTTP API `/session/status`, `/session/{id}/message` | cotail-http-discovery (see sibling) |

Layers 1–7 are read straight from the `session` table (one SELECT, no joins
except fork-point which needs a message lookup). Layer 8 is **live** state
only obtainable from a running opencode HTTP server — it is the bridge to the
HTTP-discovery ticket.

## Acceptance

- `SessionInfo` in `src/opencode/session-info.ts` is the single canonical type;
  a `SessionReport` (full) vs `SessionInfo` (core) distinction, or optional
  fields on one type — pick one and document it.
- A `--fields <list>` / `-v` selector so human output stays uncluttered while
  `--json` can carry everything.
- Each owning ticket (basic-fields, fork-*) extends the shared type rather
  than re-defining fields.
- The schema is documented in the README (a field-reference table).

## Out of scope

- The FTS index (`cotail-index`), search scoping (`cotail-search`), and
  write-side mutation (`cotail-session-mgmt`).

## Reference

- DB schema: `session` table columns (see `~/archive/doc/opencode-history.md`).
- Seed type: `src/opencode/session-info.ts`.
- Sibling: `cotail-http-discovery` — provides layer 8 (live) data.

title: get-session: resolve active session ID from an opencode PID
description:
# `cotails get-session` — resolve the active session for a running opencode process

Given an opencode PID, return its **current active session id**. This is the first
command that answers "which session is *that* opencode instance on right now?",
and it lands the foundation for a consolidated **session-information report**.

## Inputs (PID resolution order)

1. **Positional arg** — `cotails get-session <pid>` (most explicit).
2. **`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` env** — if already present (e.g. the
   `opencode-session-id-plugin` `shell.env` hook injected it into the tool
   shell cotails runs in), return it directly with no `/proc` or DB work.
3. **`OPENCODE_PID` env** — the opencode process PID (set by opencode itself
   on startup; inherited by every tool/subagent it spawns).

## PID → session mechanism (Linux `/proc`)

opencode does **not** write the active session to disk per-process, and a
TUI-mode process often runs **no HTTP listener** (so the server API is not a
reliable discovery path). The robust signal is:

1. Read `/proc/<pid>/cwd` → the project directory opencode is running in.
2. Read `/proc/<pid>/environ` → `OPENCODE_DB` (if set) to pick the right DB;
   otherwise auto-discover (`discoverDb`).
3. Query the `session` table for the **most recently `time_updated`** session
   whose `directory` matches that cwd.

This is version-agnostic: the `session` table (with `directory`,
`time_updated`) exists in **both** opencode v1 and v2 schemas, so the same
lookup serves `~/a/a/v2` (primary) and `~/a/a/v1` (legacy). The v1/v2 split
in cotails only matters for *content* (`part` vs `event` tables), not for
session metadata.

## Output / the session-information block

This ticket also introduces the canonical **`SessionInfo`** type — the start
of a standard session report that later tickets (`cotail-basic-fields`,
`cotail-fork-point`, `cotail-fork-time`) extend:

- `id`, `title`, `directory`, `slug`, `projectId`, `parentId`, `version`
- `timeCreated`, `timeUpdated` (epoch ms)

Output modes:
- default (human): session id prominent + key fields
- `--json`: full `SessionInfo` object (JSONL)
- `--id-only`: bare session id (scripting-friendly)

## Acceptance

- `cotails get-session` with no args resolves via `OPENCODE_PID`/`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`.
- `cotails get-session <pid>` resolves via `/proc`.
- `--json` and `--id-only` modes work.
- Clear errors when: PID dead, not opencode-ish, no DB, no session for cwd.
- `SessionInfo` type + query live in `src/opencode/` for reuse.

title: Implement cotails history command
description:
Implement `cotails history` per `.design/history-viewer/design.md`.

## Behavior
- Filter: `session.time_updated >= now - since` (default `--since 24h`).
- Optional `--directory <path>` substring filter; optional `--limit <n>` (0 = unlimited).
- Per session emit: id, title, directory, messages_recent, messages_total, time_updated (plus slug/time_created in machine formats).
- Counts: sum `message` (v1) + `session_message` (v2) rows — they are mutually exclusive per session, so no mode detection is needed. In-window count uses `time_created >= cutoff`. Both hit the existing `(session_id, time_created, id)` indexes.
- Sort by `time_updated DESC`.

## Output
- default: human `table` (aligned, ANSI if TTY, truncate with ellipsis, footer count line).
- `--json`: JSONL, one object per line, ISO-8601 timestamps.
- `--tsv`: tab-separated with a header line, epoch-ms timestamps.
- `--json` wins if both `--json` and `--tsv` are passed.

## `--since` parsing
Accept `Nh` / `Nd` / `Nm` and absolute ISO-8601 / epoch-ms.

## Acceptance
- `cotails history` lists the ~100 sessions active in 24h on the live DB in under 200ms.
- `cotails history --json` and `--tsv` pipe cleanly.
- `--directory` and `--limit` filter correctly.
- Verified SQL is in the design doc.
notes: Done. 106 sessions in 24h at 81ms; --json/--tsv/--directory/--limit verified; recent vs total split correct; error paths exit 2.

title: Restructure into src/ layout with entry point, bin, and subcommand dispatch
description:
Restructure from a single flat `opencotails.ts` into a domain-grouped `src/` layout, give it one working entry point, a real installable `cotails` command, and subcommand dispatch. Project is <1.0, so breaking changes are fine.

## Naming / spelling (canonicalize)
- Package: **opencoattails** (2t — matches the local dir; the current `opencotails` in package.json is a typo). CLI: **cotails**.
- Fix `package.json`: name `opencoattails`; drop bogus `"main": "index.js"` and `"module": "opencotails.js"`; add `"bin": { "cotails": "src/cli.ts" }`; realistic 0.x version; real description/keywords.
- README: consistent `opencoattails` package / `cotails` command; examples use `cotails search ...`.
- **Human action (flagged, not auto):** GitHub repo is `rektide/opencotails` (1t). Rename on GitHub to `opencoattails` and update the local remote URL.

## Target layout
```
src/
├── cli.ts                # ONE entry: shebang, main(), dispatch, top-level help
├── format.ts             # renderTable / emitJsonl / emitTsv + ANSI
├── opencode/             # abstractions · wrappers · types (version-agnostic)
│   ├── db.ts             #   discoverDb, openReadOnly, registerRegex
│   ├── types.ts          #   Session, MessageCounts, SearchHit, SearchTerms, HistoryFilter
│   ├── source.ts         #   Source interface + detectSources() factory
│   ├── v1/source.ts      #   v1 impl: message / part queries
│   └── v2/source.ts      #   v2 impl: session_message / event queries
└── commands/
    ├── search.ts         # cotails search
    └── history.ts        # cotails history (stub until cotail-history-cmd)
```
Root `opencotails.ts` is deleted; its contents split across `cli.ts`, `opencode/db.ts`, `opencode/types.ts`, `opencode/v1/source.ts`, `opencode/v2/source.ts`, `commands/search.ts`.

## Version seam (design decision)
A single DB can be mixed (v1-native + v2-native sessions during transition), so `Source` is **per-version** (`v1/` and `v2/` each implement it); `detectSources(db)` returns the set present. Commands iterate available sources and merge (history sums counts; search unions hits). This retires the global `detectMode` boolean — querying both when both are present is a correctness win for mixed DBs.

## Dispatch
`main()` in `cli.ts`: `argv[0]` → `search` | `history`; bare `cotails` or unknown subcommand prints usage (lists subcommands) and exits non-zero. `history` may print "not implemented" until cotail-history-cmd lands.

## Run / install (no-build preserved)
- Node 22+ type-stripping: `node src/cli.ts` runs directly.
- `bin: cotails → src/cli.ts` with `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang → `pnpm link --global` puts `cotails` on PATH.

## Acceptance
- `cotails search foo bar` matches today's `cotails foo bar` output (identical on v1-only DBs; may improve on mixed DBs).
- `cotails` alone prints help listing subcommands and exits non-zero.
- `cotails history` is recognized (stub ok).
- `pnpm link --global` installs a working `cotails` on PATH.
- No `opencotails.ts` at root; no `index.js`/`opencotails.js` references remain.
- `package.json` validates (name opencoattails, bin cotails→src/cli.ts, no fictional fields).
notes: Done. Restructure into src/ committed; search output + exit codes verified identical to the flat version; npm link puts cotails on PATH. Note: pnpm 11 dropped 'pnpm link --global'; 'npm link' is the working dev-install command (bin: cotails -> src/cli.ts via shebang).

title: Recent-session history viewer
description:
List sessions active within a time cutoff (default 24h) so a user can orient on *what they were recently working on and where* — complementing `search` (find by content) with `history` (find by recency).

Unlike search, history reads only session/message metadata (no body scans), so it needs **no FTS index** and runs in milliseconds against the live DB regardless of size.

Design: `.design/history-viewer/design.md` (status: decided). Verified query on the live DB: 101 sessions in 24h, sub-100ms.

## Scope (children)
- `cotail-restructure` — introduce explicit subcommand dispatcher (prerequisite; breaking change: `cotails foo` becomes `cotails search foo`).
- `cotail-history-cmd` — implement `cotails history`: cutoff filter, directory/title/recent+total message counts, table/json/tsv output.

## Out of scope
- Message-body snippets (search owns that), live `--follow` (needs the CDC engine), transcript dump (`cotail-dump` epic), FTS index (`cotail-index`).

title: File-use search: tool-call accesses
description:
List/search file paths referenced by tool calls across history.

- Extract path-like fields from tool-call parts (v1: part.data with $.type='tool', args at $.state.input — e.g. Read/Edit/Write filePath, Glob/Grep pattern/path).
- Optional glob match against the path.
- EXCLUDE paths under the session's own directory (session.directory) — cross-project focus.
- Group by session; show the session directory + the out-of-project paths hit.

Acceptance: a command lists sessions and the out-of-project file paths their tools touched, with glob filtering. v1 part reader first.

title: Cross-project file use & session relocation
description:
Work often spans projects: a session opened under project A reads/edits files in project B, then a new session gets created under B to continue. There's currently no way to see that cross-project activity, so sessions end up **misplaced** — filed where work *started* rather than where it *landed*.

Two phases joined by that use case:

1. **Discovery (read-side):** a file-use search listing file paths a session touches via tool (then shell) activity, with optional glob, **excluding paths inside the session's own `directory`**. A synthesis view ranks sessions by out-of-project activity — surfacing relocation candidates.
2. **Action (write-side):** move or copy a misplaced session into its true target project.

## Scope (children)
- `cotail-fileuse-tool` — file-use search over tool-call accesses (foundation).
- `cotail-misplaced` — misplaced-session finder (payoff of the above).
- `cotail-fileuse-shell` — extend file-use to shell-command path tokens.
- `cotail-copy-session` — copy a session into another project (safe, ships first).
- `cotail-move-session` — move/reassign a session's project (destructive, last).

## Out of scope
Search/matching semantics (`cotail-search`), transcript dump (`cotail-dump`), FTS index (`cotail-index`).

## Notes
- (1)-(3) are read-side and can ship on the current v1 DB now — tool data lives in `part` rows (`$.type='tool'`, args at `$.state.input`).
- Full v2 support needs a `session_message` reader (gap surfaced by `cotail-v2-impact`, not yet ticketed).
- (4)-(5) mutate opencode's source data; wait for the Rust/effect decision and a careful look at opencode's session/project model.
notes: Scope refined: the write-side actions (copy/move) now live under cotail-session-mgmt (the dedicated write-side epic). This epic is now DISCOVERY-ONLY: file-use search (tool + shell) + the misplaced-session finder. The misplaced finder feeds session-mgmt's move/copy as the trigger for action.

title: Session management & reparenting (write-side)
description:
The **write-side** counterpart to the read-side search/display epics: mutate session attribution in opencode's SQLite DB.

Today `cotails` is strictly read-only. opencode's CLI offers no `session move` (only `list`/`delete`), so reparenting currently means hand-rolled SQL. This epic owns safe, scripted mutation of session→project attribution.

## Scope
- **Reparent / move** — reassign a session's `project_id` (and optionally `directory`/`path`) to fix mis-attribution. Concrete trigger: coredns-dnse had 4 sessions scattered across 3 project rows (`601ddab2` = ~/src, `b663feea` = coredns-dnse, `global`); manually UPDATEd to unify under `b663feea`.
- **Project cleanup** — detect and reconcile duplicate/overlapping `project` rows for the same worktree (e.g. `global` mistakenly carrying a project-specific worktree).
- **Dry-run / preview** — show the before/after diff before writing.
- **WAL-safety discipline** — short write transactions with `busy_timeout`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, open per-op not held open. Document the conflict risk against the live opencode writer.

## Out of scope
- Read-side reporting (see `cotail-display`) and search/scoping (`cotail-search`).
- General SQLite admin (vacuum, checkpoint) — only session-attribution mutation.

## Reference
- opencode DB write warning: `~/archive/doc/opencode-store.md` §4 "What to avoid".
- Proven safe in practice: 2026-07-25 live 2-row UPDATE on `opencode-.db` while opencode ran, zero conflict (`busy_timeout=10000`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).
- Session schema: `session(project_id, directory, path, parent_id, fork_session_id, …)`.
notes: Added children: cotail-copy-session (safe, ships first) and cotail-move-session (destructive, builds on copy). Trigger context: cotail-xproject's misplaced-session finder surfaces the sessions these actions refile. cotail-move-session is the ticket form of this epic's existing reparent/move scope.

title: Understand opencode v2 impact on cotails
description:
Research spike: map opencode v2's data model and determine what v2 already provides, so the session-dump epic (`cotail-dump`) and the broader cotails feature set are grounded in v2 reality.

Questions:
1. Does v2 already dump/export transcripts? (avoid duplicating)
2. What is the canonical opencode transcript format?
3. v2 session/message/part data model vs v1 (`session`/`message`/`part`/`event`).
4. Message ordering & ordinal feasibility for range selection.
5. Net impact on cotails (schema, storage location, event-vs-table model).

Deliverable: `.design/v2.md` at the repo root.
notes:
Research complete; .design/v2.md written.

Key findings:
- v2 has NO CLI transcript dump (gap confirmed) — only a TUI palette action using formatSessionTranscript (packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:3034-3057). cotails fills a real gap.
- Canonical dump format = markdown (# title + meta block + ## User/## Shell/## Assistant joined by ---). cotails should match it for byte-compatibility.
- v2 message store = session_message table (packages/core/src/session/sql.ts:109-128); stable ordinal = seq (projector.ts:443-458). Revert creates gaps, so rank by position not raw seq.
- CRITICAL: v2-native sessions leave message/part EMPTY (only SessionV1.Event.Created emitted, session.ts:374). cotails v1 reader will silently miss v2 content -> need a session_message reader with v1 fallback.

title: Session transcript dump
description:
Dump a session's full transcript to stdout (or a file), ideally in **opencode's transcript format** so output is recognizable and portable.

## Range selection (composable)
- **By message ordinal** — e.g. `--from 5 --to 12` (5th through 12th messages, inclusive).
- **By date** — relative windows, e.g. `--from 2mo --to 2d` = everything from 2 months ago through 2 days ago, inclusive. Support units `h`, `d`, `mo` (and absolute dates if easy).
- **Mix both** — ordinal and date ranges applied together, ideally at different segments (e.g. ordinals 1-10 within a date window, or several disjoint ranges).

## Target
This ticket targets **opencode v2** (`~/a/a/v2` = `/home/rektide/archive/anomalyco/v2`) — NOT what we run yet, but the intended target. See `.design/v2.md` (produced by `cotail-v2-impact`) for the v2 data model + transcript format, and to confirm v2 doesn't already ship a dump we'd be duplicating.

## Depends on
- `cotail-v2-impact` — research prerequisite.
notes: Confirmed via cotail-v2-impact: v2 ships no CLI dump (TUI-only), so this epic fills a real gap. Target format = formatSessionTranscript markdown (packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:3034-3057); read v2 from session_message (seq ordinal), fall back to message/part for v1. See .design/v2.md.

title: Show other low-effort session fields
description:
Several useful columns on the `session` table are a single SELECT + render away (no joins, no new logic). Batch them as optional display enrichments:

- `model` — model name (e.g. `glm-5.2`).
- `agent` — agent name.
- `version` — opencode version that ran the session.
- `cost` (real) — session cost in USD.
- `tokens_input`, `tokens_output`, `tokens_reasoning`, `tokens_cache_read`, `tokens_cache_write` — token usage.
- `summary_files`, `summary_additions`, `summary_deletions` — git diff summary stats.
- `share_url` — share link (if set).
- `workspace_id` — workspace.

Implementation notes:
- All are direct columns on `session`; add to the existing SELECTs in `buildTitleQuery` / `buildPartQuery`.
- Render compactly in human view (consider a `--verbose`/`-v` flag to avoid clutter, or a `--fields` selector). Always include in `--json`.
- Each can land independently if desired.

Acceptance: at least model + cost + token totals render in `--json` and (optionally, behind a flag) in human output.

title: Search & scoping
description:
The **query/matching read-side**: how users find and scope sessions against the source opencode DB (and later the FTS index).

Scope:
- **Regex matching** — DONE (case-insensitive JS regex via custom `re()`; `-F`/`--fixed-strings`, `-s`/`--case-sensitive`).
- **Term semantics** — currently strict AND of all terms; consider OR, phrase/exact, negation.
- **Scoping filters** — `--directory`, `--session <id>`, `--project <id>` (source schema supports all three via `session.directory` / `session.id` / `session.project_id`).
- **Type filter** — text/reasoning/tool exists; consider message-role scoping.

Out of scope: reporting/display fields (see `cotail-display`) and the FTS index write-path (see `cotail-index`). Scoping-by-directory is the filter counterpart to the `cotail-directory` display ticket.

title: Show last fork point (prev reply <-> fork reply, with timestamps)
description:
Given `session.fork_message_id` (the message at the divergence boundary), render the two turns flanking it:

- the **previous prompt + reply** immediately before the boundary, with its `time_created` stamp;
- the **fork prompt + reply** at/after the boundary, with its `time_created` stamp.

Fetch turns from `message`/`part` (v1) or `event` filtered to `message.part.updated.1` (v2) — see the README "V2 event fallback" section for the table/field mapping.

Acceptance: for a forked session, both boundary turns render with timestamps in human and json output.

title: Show last fork time
description:
A session forks via `session.fork_session_id` (parent) + `session.fork_message_id` (divergence point).

"Last fork time" = the most recent fork event touching this session. Two interpretations:
1. This session forked from its parent (its own `time_created` when `fork_session_id` is set).
2. A child forked FROM this session (`max(time_created)` over sessions where `fork_session_id = this.id`).

Decision needed: default to interpretation 2 (latest fork touching the session); show interpretation 1 when set.

Acceptance: fork time rendered (human + json) where fork lineage exists; omitted when none.

title: Show session first-created time
description:
Add `session.time_created` to results alongside the existing `updated` timestamp.

- Human view: distinguish created vs updated (show both compactly).
- `--json`: expose a `created` field.

Acceptance: first-created timestamp from `session.time_created` appears in both human and json output.
notes:
Implemented in opencotails.ts:
- Added `created` = datetime(time_created/1000) to both SELECTs.
- renderHuman shows `created → updated` when they differ, else the single timestamp.
- `--json` exposes `created` (alongside `updated`).

Verified across part search, --title-only, and --json.

title: Copy a session into another project
description:
Non-destructive: clone a session (and its fork lineage?) into a target project/directory — reassigning project_id/directory on the copy, original intact. Decide whether the copy lives in opencode's DB (new session) or a cotails-owned store. Ship before move (safe, reversible).

Acceptance: copy <session> --to <project/dir> produces a session filed under the target without altering the original.

title: Move a session to another project
description:
Destructive: reassign a session's project_id/directory to a target (≈ copy + delete original, or a direct update). Safeguards: dry-run, confirmation, move record. Depends on cotail-copy-session.

Acceptance: move <session> --to <project/dir> refiles the session under the target; original removed/archived with confirmation.

title: File-use search: shell-command accesses
description:
Extend file-use extraction to shell commands: parse the command string for path tokens (args of cd/cat/cp/mv/editors, redirects). Same glob + exclude-in-project filtering as cotail-fileuse-tool. Lower frequency than tool accesses but catches activity the structured tools miss.

Depends on cotail-fileuse-tool.

Acceptance: shell-command path tokens appear in the file-use listing alongside tool paths.

title: Misplaced-session finder
description:
Synthesis view over file-use data: rank sessions by the share/count of file activity OUTSIDE session.directory. Surface "filed under A but most access is in B" candidates, inferring the likely target directory from the dominant external paths. Default threshold + override flag.

Depends on cotail-fileuse-tool.

Acceptance: a command lists sessions whose out-of-project file activity exceeds a threshold, with the inferred target directory.

title: Port cotails to Rust
description:
Rewrite cotails as a Rust project: the opencode source DB and the cotails FTS index read via the `turso` crate (or `rusqlite`), clap-v4 CLI, figment2 config, tracing. Rust is a natural fit for a fast local search/index tool and matches the broader toolchain.

Candidate scope:
- Read-only source-DB access (regex + display) reimplemented in Rust.
- Phase 1 FTS index (`cotail-index`) as a separate owned DB.
- Incremental indexing + `status`.

## ⚠️ Language decision is UNRESOLVED
We have NOT decided whether cotails's future home is **Rust** or **effect.ts**. This epic and `cotail-effect` are the two parallel candidate paths; at most one will proceed.

### Before starting this epic, ask the user:
1. **Commit for real?** — are we committing to Rust as the production path, or
2. **Prototype only?** — just spike it in Rust to learn/compare, or
3. **Hold and compare?** — pause and weigh it against the effect.ts path first.

Do not begin implementation until the user has answered. See the twin epic `cotail-effect`.

title: Port cotails to effect.ts
description:
Adopt [effect.ts](https://effect.website) as the future home for cotails: structured concurrency, Layers/Services for the DB + index + config, typed errors, and a config layer (figment2/clap-style ergonomics on the TS side).

Candidate scope:
- Model the opencode source DB and the cotails FTS index DB as Effect Services/Layers.
- Port the existing regex search + display features into the Effect app.
- Build the Phase 1 FTS index path (`cotail-index`) on top.

## ⚠️ Language decision is UNRESOLVED
We have NOT decided whether cotails's future home is **Rust** or **effect.ts**. This epic and `cotail-rust` are the two parallel candidate paths; at most one will proceed.

### Before starting this epic, ask the user:
1. **Commit for real?** — are we committing to effect.ts as the production path, or
2. **Prototype only?** — just spike it in effect.ts to learn/compare, or
3. **Hold and compare?** — pause and weigh it against the Rust path first.

Do not begin implementation until the user has answered. See the twin epic `cotail-rust`.

title: FTS index (Phase 1)
description:
**Phase 1: the FTS index write-path.** Move from ~5s regex scans of the 4.8 GB source DB to milliseconds-scale FTS5 MATCH.

Scope:
- Owned cotails index DB (~/.local/share/cotails/index.db, Turso/SQLite FTS5) — see README architecture + planned schema.
- `cotails index` — build + incremental indexing keyed on `session.time_updated`.
- Scopable indexing: --session, --directory, --project, --since.
- `cotails status` — coverage, freshness, stale-session count, index size.

Produces the index that `cotail-search` queries. Engine choice (Rust turso vs effect.ts) is gated by `cotail-rust` / `cotail-effect`.
